parallel.requirements: The run recognized that it had to clone the behavior of the bundled dog DNS client from docs and CLI observation only, without using source, internet, wrapping, or binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent initially explored and built a reusable fake-DNS toolkit, then delegated seven behavior-spec areas to child agents while keeping the later implementation and integration work for after the specs.
parallel.implementation: No production reimplementation was written. The completed work was probe infrastructure and two research specs for CLI parsing and query wire behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained probe scripts, the two spec files, original docs/assets, and an empty or non-substantive src directory; it did not include a buildable submitted implementation or compile script.
parallel.verification: The parent performed probe-based checks of the reference binary and children performed local probes, but no integrated verification of a new executable occurred.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Five needed behavior-spec children were aborted and the implementation, integration, differential testing, and build-delivery stages were never reached before timeout.

serial.requirements: The serial agent identified the same clean-room reimplementation requirement and used the docs plus normal CLI execution of the supplied binary as its evidence source.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent owned all probing, specification, implementation, testing, and delivery work through a todo list; there were no child agents or delegated work products.
serial.implementation: The serial run produced increasingly capable Python probe servers and logs under /workspace/test but did not begin a new Rust, Go, C, or script implementation of dog.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact contained test harness files, certificates, logs, docs, completions, and the original executable, but no new buildable dog replacement or compile script.
serial.verification: Verification consisted of reference-binary probing against local DNS, TCP, TLS, and DoH servers; no candidate implementation was built or compared.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: At cancellation, the serial agent was still exploring resolver and EDNS details, with implementation, differential testing, and compile-script tasks pending.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent understood the clean-room task and captured the required no-source, no-wrapper, no-disassembly constraints before probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent received and followed the same prompt constraints while using the binary and bundled documentation as the source of behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirement-recognition difference; the divergence was in execution strategy, not task interpretation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed the problem into seven child-owned behavior-spec assignments and reserved implementation for a later parent/implementation phase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt kept all research, implementation, and build ownership inside one main agent with no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel made a broad spec swarm the gating phase; serial had no cross-agent ownership boundary and simply advanced the probe list itself.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child briefs were specific and referenced a shared briefing and port ranges; the issue was not missing task context or an interface contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run accumulated context in one trajectory and therefore had no inter-agent handoff or child-brief boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced many context-transfer surfaces but the observable failure was cancellation before most results returned; serial avoided handoffs but still did not deliver.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a shared Python probe toolkit, a briefing, and two completed behavior specs, but did not write the required replacement implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote Python DNS, TCP, TLS, and DoH probe servers and used them extensively, but also did not write the required replacement implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more structured delegated spec artifacts; serial had more continuous solo probing. Neither path crossed into a compilable solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The AgentSwarm returned only two completed children and five aborted children after an active-turn cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child result lifecycle; its final raw event is a main-agent active-turn cancellation during a probe step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel-specific failure was early termination of active child work, while serial had no comparable child results to retrieve or join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple children wrote probe scripts/spec files in the shared workspace, but the retained evidence shows no harmful overwrite or consumed contaminated artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial workspace contained only one agent's test harnesses, certificates, and logs, with no competing writes from other actors.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-state exposure but no proven collision; both final artifacts were research/probe workspaces rather than integrated deliveries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified the reference binary and received two child spec summaries, but never tested a built replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial conducted extensive reference-binary probes including record formats, transports, TLS, DoH, and resolver handling, but never verified a replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial run accumulated more direct probe evidence in one context; the parallel run had two completed child findings but no integrated acceptance loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The run timed out after using seven subagents; cancellation arrived during the spec swarm before implementation and build-delivery stages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also timed out, but its budget was spent in a single long probing sequence with later implementation tasks still pending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget before a buildable solution, but only parallel lost active child work through the swarm cancellation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations failed the same way: `solution_passed` is false, the evaluator completed, the error code is `compile_failed`, and all 1722 tests were not run. The parallel run has an adverse child-lifecycle failure because its spec swarm was canceled with five children unfinished, but the serial control also never produced a buildable implementation, so there is no outcome difference to explain.
parallel_contributors: The AgentSwarm was canceled after only two of seven behavior-spec children completed, preventing the parent from using the full planned spec set.
The final parallel artifact contained probes and two spec files rather than a compilable reimplementation.
serial_contributors: The serial agent spent the run on direct probing and was still running resolver and EDNS probes at cancellation.
The final serial artifact contained test harnesses and generated certificates/logs rather than a compilable reimplementation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial gathered some DoH, resolver, TLS, and record-format observations itself, while parallel delegated much of that work and lost five unfinished child results.
Neither run reached source implementation, integration, or compile-script delivery.

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly planned to implement after the spec phase, so implementation was assigned to a later stage rather than left ownerless.
No multiple completed component implementations existed that needed an unassigned integration owner.
No complete implementation pieces or entry point were ready for final packaging, so assembly was not the first failed boundary.
The parent retained the end-to-end plan across specs, implementation, testing, and build; the run stopped before that pipeline could proceed.
The initial toolkit and briefing enabled later parallel probing; there is no separate mandatory preflight gate shown as the direct adverse boundary.
The investigation phase was actively parallelized and not completed before implementation; the concrete failure is early cancellation of active child work.
The indispensable implementation path was intended after the spec swarm; the direct observable boundary is cancellation before child results finalized.
Seven children and timeout are budget signals, but the taxonomy requires choosing the direct cancellation boundary for this same chain.
No single child assignment is shown to be uniquely oversized relative to siblings; five distinct children were stopped by the same cancellation.
The child prompts included the clean-room rules, shared briefing requirement, output file, port range, exact behaviors to probe, and delivery expectations.
The delegated work products were independent behavior specs, not separately implemented components that needed a missing interoperability contract.
No known finding is shown to disappear in transfer; two completed child summaries were returned in the swarm result.
The parent did not receive an oversized complete handoff and then fail to reduce it; the run ended at cancellation.
No receiver consumed a superseded child result or old workspace description before taking an inconsistent next step.
No incompatible child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent never presented or accepted the task as complete; the run was canceled before whole-task delivery.
There was no replacement or retry actor repeating earlier work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: An executed seven-child AgentSwarm was explicitly canceled while five needed child spec tasks were still active and unfinished.
candidates.realized_consequence: Only two of seven planned specs were available; five behavior areas lacked finalized child reports, and the parent never reached implementation, integration, or build delivery.
candidates.near_match_reason: The lack of recovery is downstream of the same terminal cancellation; the directly evidenced and corrective boundary is not stopping active children before results finalize.

candidates.reason: No complete implementation candidate or mutually compatible component set was ready for final placement before the run ended.
No child implementation or code change was merged after a relevant integrated verification pass.
No delegated implementation completed or became retrievable; the completed child outputs were research specifications.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent.
The parent received the cancellation result only at terminal closure, so takeover is not a distinct observable decision separate from the early termination chain.
The two completed child results were returned inside the terminal swarm result; there is no later parent decision that ignored them.
The parent was waiting on an active AgentSwarm and the explicit cancellation, not an uninspected available-progress decision, is the direct boundary.
Children wrote probes and specs for separate research areas, not competing implementation files with overlapping ownership.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file in a way that required reconciliation.
No non-entry source file produced or owned by one agent was replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewritten by another.
The run did not produce a required executable or entry-point source deliverable that another actor overwrote.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree work or invalidated provenance.
Shared workspace writes occurred, but there is no concrete unstable-state or provenance failure beyond the canceled spec swarm.
Probe artifacts and transient servers are visible, but no actor consumed another actor's generated artifact as stable reference input causing contamination.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent launched seven needed spec children, but the active swarm was canceled before five children finalized their work.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Five behavior areas lacked finalized child reports, leaving the parent without the intended complete spec set and no completed implementation or build delivery.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The lack of recovery is a downstream effect of terminal cancellation, not a separate post-failure takeover decision.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the explicit child cancellation clears the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The timeout, missing implementation, missing recovery, and absent finalization are treated as one cancellation chain rather than separate retained labels.
